_readme: Declared state of the merge and deploy control plane for CleanExpo/Synthex.
Written for Gruen Standard v1.1 Phase 0.0 (docs/specs/gruen-standard/spec.md, section 7).
expected          - the value the repository MUST have right now. scripts/check-repo-controls.mjs
fails if the live value differs. This is the DRIFT assert.
phase_0_0_target  - the value Phase 0.0 requires. null means Phase 0.0 does not move this control;
it is declared only so that drift in it is detected.
gate              - who can change it. 'founder' means it needs repo-admin rights this repo's
When a founder closes a Phase 0.0 item, they update 'expected' to match the new reality in the
same PR. An 'expected' that still differs from 'phase_0_0_target' is an OPEN GAP and is reported
Do NOT set 'expected' to the target as a way of 'declaring intent'. This file describes what is,
not what is wished for; the target column is the only place a wish belongs.
observed_by: read-only gh api reads; no PATCH/PUT/POST/DELETE was issued

repo.owner_type.note: Load-bearing. CleanExpo is a personal account, not an Organization, so GitHub's audit-log API (orgs/{org}/audit-log) does not exist for this repo. The Phase 0.0 anchor 'the refused merge, in GitHub's own audit log' cannot be produced from this account type. See docs/specs/gruen-standard/phase-0-0-founder-runbook.md item P7.

repo.default_branch.note: The branch every protection.* control below is read from. Two separate guards, because they catch different things. (1) This control compares the LIVE default branch against `expected`, so moving the repository's default branch is drift. (2) The script separately refuses to run at all unless the `default_branch` input at the top of this file equals the live default branch — without that, the input could be pointed at `sandbox` while this control still expected and observed `main`, and every protection value would then describe a branch pull requests do not target. The first catches the repository changing; the second catches the declaration lying about which branch it audited.

repo.allow_auto_merge.note: Repo-wide auto-merge off. Matches spec section 4 E1 ('while repo-wide auto-merge was off') - PR #822 did not use it.

protection.required_status_checks.strict.note: strict=false means a PR can merge against a stale base. Not named by Phase 0.0.

protection.required_status_checks.contex.note: Only 2 of ci.yml's 6 jobs are required to merge. Type Check, Unit Tests, Auth Coverage Ratchet and Pipeline Smoke Tests (blocking) are NOT required. Not named by Phase 0.0; recorded so that silently dropping Build or Lint is detected.

protection.enforce_admins.note: Admins are subject to branch protection on main.

protection.required_signatures.note: Unsigned commits are accepted on main. This is the only GitHub control that refuses a commit for being unattributable, but Phase 0.0 does not name it, so no target is declared here. Raised as runbook item P8 for a founder ruling.

protection.lock_branch.note: Declared for drift only. A standing freeze would set this true.

protection.reviews.required_approving_re.note: Read from the sub-resource. NOTE: the top-level protection payload omits required_pull_request_reviews entirely on this repo, so a check that reads only the top-level endpoint would conclude reviews are unconfigured. The sub-resource is authoritative.

protection.reviews.dismiss_stale_reviews.note: An approval survives a new push. Not named by Phase 0.0.

protection.reviews.require_last_push_app.note: The identity that pushed last can also be the approver. Directly adjacent to Phase 0.0's self-review concern, but Phase 0.0 names the Production ENVIRONMENT rule, not this one. Raised as runbook item P9.

branches.protected.note: Two protected branches. `sandbox` is protected in name only: zero required contexts, enforce_admins false, and allow_force_pushes AND allow_deletions both TRUE. It is not a deploy branch, so Phase 0.0 does not reach it. Declared so a new protected branch, or a change to sandbox, is detected. NOTE: `develop` IS a deploy branch in deploy.yml (on.push.branches) and is not protected at all.

legacy.branch_protection_json.present.note: OPEN GAP, and a judgement call: the spec does not name this file, so the target here is mine, not the spec's, and a founder may set it to null instead. `.github/branch-protection.json` is a tracked second protection-as-code file added 2025-08-12 (commit 95679169b). Every branch-protection claim in it is FALSE against the live repository and nothing reads it. Leaving it beside this file gives the repo two declarations of the merge control plane that disagree. Full divergence table: runbook item P12.

legacy.branch_protection_json.reader_cou.note: Files under .github/workflows/, scripts/ or package.json that read .github/branch-protection.json. Zero: it is applied by nothing. Spec section 7 item 0.2 states the principle - 'an uncalled gate is testimony of a control that does not operate'. This file is the documentation-layer instance of exactly that.

rulesets.count.note: No repository rulesets exist; branch protection is the only merge control.

environment.Production.can_admins_bypass.note: OPEN GAP. Spec section 4 E3 and Phase 0.0. deploy.yml's deploy-production job targets environment 'production', which GitHub resolves case-insensitively to this 'Production' environment (verified by read-back).

environment.Production.prevent_self_revi.note: OPEN GAP. Spec section 4 E3 and Phase 0.0. The single required reviewer is CleanExpo, who is also the merging identity, so the production deploy approval is self-granted.

environment.Production.required_reviewer.note: Sole reviewer. Phase 0.0 does not add a second reviewer; it removes self-review, which on a single-reviewer rule means the deploy must be approved by someone other than the merger.

environment.count.note: 14 environments exist; 13 of them have zero protection rules, including 7 named 'Production - synthex*' created by the Vercel git integration. Declared so that a NEW unprotected deploy surface appearing is detected. Spec section 4 E4.

actions.variable.DEPLOY_INHIBIT.value.note: OPEN GAP. Spec section 4 E2: actions/variables returns total_count 0, so the value is null (the variable does not exist). The switch is read at .github/workflows/deploy.yml:119 as `vars.DEPLOY_INHIBIT != 'true'`, so an unset variable evaluates to '' and the production deploy job runs. The VALUE is declared, not merely the variable's existence: only the exact string 'true' inhibits a deploy, so a variable holding 'false', 'TRUE' or '1' would satisfy an existence check while production still deployed. P1 is the founder creating this variable, which is exactly when a name-only control would have started reporting an armed kill-switch that was not armed.

actions.secret.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK.exists.note: OPEN GAP. Spec section 4 E4 and Phase 0.0 ('remove or authenticate the dormant VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK'). Secret last updated 2025-08-04T05:15:35Z and referenced by ZERO workflows (grep over .github returns no hits). 'Authenticate' is not observable from outside GitHub, so the machine-checkable target is removal.

workflow.deploy.production_if_condition.note: The exact `if:` on the deploy-production job in .github/workflows/deploy.yml, verbatim. Replaces an earlier boolean 'does this condition mention DEPLOY_INHIBIT', which a condition could satisfy while defeating it: `&& (vars.DEPLOY_INHIBIT != 'true' || always())` contains the guard and always runs. A substring cannot decide a boolean expression, so the whole condition is declared and ANY edit to it is drift. Deliberately strict: this is the one line between a push to main and a production deploy, and a human should look at every change to it. Editing it legitimately means updating this string in the same PR.

workflow.deploy.production_environment_b.note: Asserts the deploy-production job in .github/workflows/deploy.yml still binds `environment: name: production`. The four environment.Production.* controls audit GitHub's copy of that environment; this is the only one that asks whether the production deploy job is still attached to it. Without it, moving the job to another environment silently detaches the required-reviewer rule while every environment control keeps matching.

workflow.deploy.vercel_deploy_hook_refer.note: Number of .github files referencing VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK. Zero today, which is exactly why the secret is dormant-and-unauthenticated rather than in use.
